Billion Rand Mega Project

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
An R 11 biliion mega city project mismangaged to smithereens

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche investigates what happened to the R 11 billion meant to create a state of the art mega city on the outskirts of former gold mining town Randfontein. It seems a shady so-called developer with close political ties to Paul Mashatile secured the bag and ran with it - leaving a trail of unpaid contractors in the dust along with the "mega city" project.

Summary:
Who is Sam Mhlaba? He is the sole director of self-titled business - Sam Comfort Mhlaba or SCM Holdings. But there's nothing comforting about the work Sam has executed on the R 11 billion Montrose Mega City project. The brochure made big money promises and in an interview Sam even said Montrose Mega City would be a step up from the department of human settlements flagship baby - Cosmo City.
However, on the ground - the brochure isnt matching up at all because 7 years after its inception over 1000 units were started but none have been completed in 6 fiscal years of works. It's alleged Sam has received R 410 million on the project thus far but the Gauteng Partnership Fund aint budging when it comes to clarifying exatly how much in taxpayer Rands has been dispensed to this incompetent developer.

Further information:
Cosmo City, it’s the government’s flagship mega city housing development initiated in 2001.
Over 1000 hectares of land has been transformed into this - over 12500 mixed housing units,
schools, parks, shopping malls, churches and a population of over 70 000.

In 2014, the department of human settlements was struggling to deliver on small housing
projects but took the bold decision all public housing was to be delivered in ‘megaprojects’,
also referred to as ‘catalytic projects’.

Mega Projects are a R100-billion economic corridor investment that aims to deliver more than 800
000 houses within 30 residential developments spread across the five development corridors in
Gauteng.

Viz: drone shots of different mega cities - dramatic music underneath - these are available on
Facebook and YouTube - department of human settlements
But with over 4000 informal settlements nationally and a housing backlog spanning decades -
can mega projects meet the demand fast enough

https://www.news24.com/citypress/news/r11bn-revitalisation-programme-on-track-in-
randfontein-20171110

In 2017, Deputy President - Paul Mashatile - was the Gauteng Human Settlements MEC.
He’s pictured here at a soil turning ceremony to launch the Montrose Mega City
development in Randfontein

Viz: Zoom into Paul …isolate bring his image forward

To Mashatile’s left is the project developer awarded the R 11 billion project, Sam Comfort
Mhlaba of SCM Holdings

Viz: Zoom into Sam …isolate bring his image forward …stamp R 11 billion across Sam

Montrose Mega City development is situated just under an hour from Johannesburg CBD
in defiance of the City’s own policy which states”housing should be developed along
transport corridors and areas with economic potential.

It’s ghostly silent, with this disused train station - years ago the gold mines and related
businesses closed down simultaneously.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): An R 11 biliion mega city project mismangaged to smithereens
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche investigates what happened to the R 11 billion meant to create a state of the art mega city on the outskirts of former gold mining town Randfontein. It seems a shady so-called developer with close political ties to Paul Mashatile secured the bag and ran with it - leaving a trail of unpaid contractors in the dust along with the "mega city" project.
metadata.Summary: Who is Sam Mhlaba? He is the sole director of self-titled business - Sam Comfort Mhlaba or SCM Holdings. But there's nothing comforting about the work Sam has executed on the R 11 billion Montrose Mega City project. The brochure made big money promises and in an interview Sam even said Montrose Mega City would be a step up from the department of human settlements flagship baby - Cosmo City. However, on the ground - the brochure isnt matching up at all because 7 years after its inception over 1000 units were started but none have been completed in 6 fiscal years of works. It's alleged Sam has received R 410 million on the project thus far but the Gauteng Partnership Fund aint budging when it comes to clarifying exatly how much in taxpayer Rands has been dispensed to this incompetent developer.
metadata.Further information: Cosmo City, it’s the government’s flagship mega city housing development initiated in 2001. Over 1000 hectares of land has been transformed into this - over 12500 mixed housing units, schools, parks, shopping malls, churches and a population of over 70 000. In 2014, the department of human settlements was struggling to deliver on small housing projects but took the bold decision all public housing was to be delivered in ‘megaprojects’, also referred to as ‘catalytic projects’. Mega Projects are a R100-billion economic corridor investment that aims to deliver more than 800 000 houses within 30 residential developments spread across the five development corridors in Gauteng. Viz: drone shots of different mega cities - dramatic music underneath - these are available on Facebook and YouTube - department of human settlements But with over 4000 informal settlements nationally and a housing backlog spanning decades - can mega projects meet the demand fast enough https://www.news24.com/citypress/news/r11bn-revitalisation-programme-on-track-in- randfontein-20171110 In 2017, Deputy President - Paul Mashatile - was the Gauteng Human Settlements MEC. He’s pictured here at a soil turning ceremony to launch the Montrose Mega City development in Randfontein Viz: Zoom into Paul …isolate bring his image forward To Mashatile’s left is the project developer awarded the R 11 billion project, Sam Comfort Mhlaba of SCM Holdings Viz: Zoom into Sam …isolate bring his image forward …stamp R 11 billion across Sam Montrose Mega City development is situated just under an hour from Johannesburg CBD in defiance of the City’s own policy which states”housing should be developed along transport corridors and areas with economic potential. It’s ghostly silent, with this disused train station - years ago the gold mines and related businesses closed down simultaneously.
